## Reader decision and overlap audit

The existing `/blog/system-boundary-observability/` page already owns the broad reader question: when native agent telemetry is enough, when independent system observation is needed, and how the two boundaries relate. A new keyword variant would have duplicated that decision.

The refresh therefore kept the same canonical URL and added information that was expensive to reconstruct from ordinary search results:

- a four-layer evidence model separating intent/session, tool protocol, system execution, and provider traffic;
- an exact AgentSight v1.0.30 map of what the OpenTelemetry exporter emits versus what remains in AgentSight-native provenance;
- the current grouping/content/privacy boundaries of the OTel exporter;
- the explicit current limitation that standard `execute_tool`, `invoke_agent`, `invoke_workflow`, and `plan` spans are not emitted yet;
- a practical investigation table showing which evidence source should be used first for model cost, tool intent, slow commands, extension effects, and OTel pipeline integration.

The existing upstream-agent research pins were retained rather than silently rewritten: Gemini CLI commit `cf22ac7e86f3dcf528e3ae591fec1c03090a49f8` and Codex commit `3aae5d885bac39c1262491aa3fd100dfd8b3919f`. AgentSight-specific claims were revalidated against exact v1.0.30 commit `934f441eff8ca210807333633f47b2efcb8cd020`, especially `docs/otel.md`, the README, and the OTel sink implementation.
